items.title: Compaction results have no transition, ordering, or retry-race oracle
items.statement: ATS-017 enumerates result states but does not specify legal transitions, event/result ordering, correlation identity, duplicate completion handling, or what must happen when cancel and retry overlap. A suite can cover every named label while missing stale or contradictory state under concurrent commands.
items.impact: The GUI can show a terminal state that belongs to an earlier attempt, or a retry can compact twice without a failing oracle.

evidence.exact_quote: - Tests cover already_running, cancelled, no_op, degraded, unavailable, retry_scheduled, completed, and failed result states.

items.title: Failed compaction lacks atomicity and rollback proof
items.statement: A visible failed/degraded state is required, but there is no oracle proving that partial summary writes, context replacement, token accounting, and storage metadata remain atomic or are restored after failure. Retry behavior after a partially applied compaction is also unspecified.
items.impact: A failed operation can silently corrupt or truncate the active context while still satisfying visible failure coverage.

evidence.exact_quote: - Failure/degraded compaction produces a visible user-facing state and event contract.

items.title: Pointer-only Compact Now coverage omits accessible entry paths
items.statement: The required GUI coverage is framed as hover, click, and selection. It does not require keyboard focus/activation, screen-reader naming and state announcements, non-hover disclosure on touch, focus restoration, or reduced-motion/high-contrast behavior.
items.impact: The manual compaction entry point may pass GUI tests while remaining unavailable or misleading to keyboard, assistive-technology, or touch users.

evidence.exact_quote: - Compact Now click in the chat context circle is covered by GUI tests, not assumed from slash command support.

items.title: Slash-command parity is asserted without a shared observable contract
items.statement: The prose names `/compact` parity but never defines which preconditions, result payloads, events, cancellation semantics, permission checks, and user-visible states must be identical versus intentionally channel-specific. The two callers can diverge while both are individually tested.
items.impact: Chat-circle and slash-command callers may produce different authority or recovery outcomes with no parity oracle.

evidence.exact_quote: click reveal/selection of Compact Now before dispatch to `cmd.chat.compact_context`; `/compact` parity;

items.title: Compaction usage details lack privacy and localization oracles
items.statement: ATS-017 requires Usage, Tokens, Cost, and More Details display but does not constrain sensitive prompt/account data, retention, telemetry redaction, locale-specific currency/number formatting, text expansion, or translated accessible names.
items.impact: Tests may certify a detail view that leaks data or misstates cost and token values outside the default locale.

evidence.exact_quote: Compaction acceptance tests cover the chat context circle hover display for Usage, Tokens, Cost, and More Details;

items.title: Hover is explicitly prohibited from dispatching compaction
items.statement: The core closes the misleading-hover authority gap by making hover disclosure non-dispatching and requiring the user to choose Compact Now before command dispatch.

evidence.exact_quote: - Do not dispatch compaction from hover alone.

items.title: DRY setting has no in-flight snapshot or concurrent-write semantics
items.statement: The toggle is constrained to two stored values, but the plan does not define when a run snapshots the effective value, how multi-window or external settings writes are serialized, or whether changing the toggle can alter an already-built Instruction Bundle.
items.impact: One run can contain mixed DRY behavior, and the receipt may not prove which effective state governed each prompt route.

evidence.exact_quote: - The Settings command and wiring fixture proves the toggle writes only enabled or disabled_by_user and displays the exact explanatory copy.

items.title: DRY receipt fields and hashes are not enumerated
items.statement: The canonical text asks for receipt fields and hashes but supplies no required field set, hash input/canonicalization algorithm, correlation key, or mutation oracle. This makes a passing receipt non-falsifiable and weakens support diagnosis.
items.impact: Implementations can emit incompatible or self-referential receipts that nominally satisfy the prose but cannot prove route identity or effective policy.

evidence.exact_quote: prompt routes, absence of shadow prompt-builder-local DRY prose, receipt fields and hashes, missing/stale rules

items.title: Shared Instruction Bundle consumption lacks input-authenticity tests
items.statement: Routing every consumer through one bundle does not prove that canonical owner/source references, rule contents, hashes, and precedence are authentic or protected against path substitution, stale-cache injection, malformed content, and untrusted project text masquerading as authority.
items.impact: A single compromised shared bundle can consistently propagate attacker-controlled instructions to every listed prompt route.

evidence.exact_quote: - All prompt routes consume one shared Instruction Bundle route.

items.title: DRY toggle persistence failure and rollback are untested
items.statement: The wiring fixture proves successful writes only. It does not cover permission denial, disk-full, corrupt configuration, interrupted atomic replace, acknowledgement loss, or rollback when persisted and displayed states disagree.
items.impact: Settings can report DRY disabled while runtime remains enabled, or vice versa, with no required recovery or user warning.

evidence.exact_quote: - The Settings command and wiring fixture proves the toggle writes only enabled or disabled_by_user and displays the exact explanatory copy.

items.title: DRY migration and route completeness are unspecified
items.statement: The plan checks a fixed set of current routes and stale local prose, but defines neither discovery of newly added prompt consumers nor migration of existing opt-in/boolean/unknown settings and cached local rule copies. Future callers and older profiles can bypass the shared route silently.
items.impact: Upgrades or new prompt routes can create shadow behavior despite the static conformance suite passing.

evidence.exact_quote: Bundle routing for Assistant, Interview, Orchestrator, delegated child-run, document-builder, and code-generation

items.title: Disabling DRY does not weaken independent authority boundaries
items.statement: The core expressly preserves user instructions, safety, secret handling, source authority, governance, permissions, and source-control hygiene when DRY is off.

evidence.exact_quote: - Do not treat disabled DRY as permission to bypass explicit instructions, safety, secrets, source authority, governance, permissions, or source-control hygiene.

items.title: Container host proof omits provenance, isolation, and secret-boundary tests
items.statement: ATS-019 records image/build and access refs but does not require image provenance or digest verification, least-privilege mounts, network isolation, secret injection/redaction, hostile artifact handling, URL credential stripping, or tenant separation.
items.impact: A containerized test can execute untrusted content with excessive host access or leak credentials while producing a structurally valid TestRunReceipt.

evidence.exact_quote: runtime_context_ref, optional compose_scenario_ref, image/build refs, port/access URL refs, preflight receipt ref,

items.title: Cleanup and retain-on-failure have no lifecycle or destructive-action contract
items.statement: The receipt names cleanup and retention but does not define cleanup idempotency, scope authorization, partial-cleanup recovery, deletion verification, retry/backoff, retention TTL, quota behavior, user override, or which artifacts survive cleanup.
items.impact: Cleanup can delete another run's resources or leave secret-bearing hosts and artifacts indefinitely without invalidating success.

evidence.exact_quote: launch receipt ref, harness probe receipt ref, cleanup receipt ref, retain-on-failure state, evidence refs, visual

items.title: Host assignment lacks contention, capacity, and port-collision tests
items.statement: The contract records an assigned host and ports but has no tests for two runs claiming one host/profile, reservation expiry, launch cancellation races, port reuse, oversubscription, resource exhaustion, noisy neighbors, backpressure, or maximum evidence size.
items.impact: Parallel and high-volume runs can cross-wire evidence, collide on access endpoints, or hang indefinitely while single-run fixtures pass.

evidence.exact_quote: host_profile_id, host_instance_ref or host_instance_id, host_assignment_ref or host_assignment_id, runtime_family,

items.title: Container adapter compatibility and receipt evolution are unbounded
items.statement: The broader adapter family is mentioned without supported runtime/Compose versions, capability negotiation, schema-version rules, unknown-field behavior, backward migration, or required behavior when producer and consumer versions differ.
items.impact: A valid receipt or host profile from one adapter version may be rejected or misinterpreted by another without a blocked result.

evidence.exact_quote: for non-Compose and runtime-specific hosts. TestRunReceipt proves containerized execution with host_capability_ref,

items.title: Container receipts lack operational correlation and bounded diagnostics
items.statement: The field list has refs but no required run/attempt correlation, timestamps and clock semantics, causal error codes, redacted diagnostic envelope, liveness timeout, metric thresholds, or support-export behavior.
items.impact: Operators cannot distinguish a stale receipt from the current attempt or diagnose which lifecycle stage failed without inspecting unsafe raw logs.

evidence.exact_quote: evidence refs, and blocker payload.

items.title: Running container is not accepted as test success
items.statement: The core explicitly rejects infrastructure liveness as completion and requires ATS evidence and receipts.

evidence.exact_quote: - Do not treat a running container as test completion or success without ATS evidence and receipts.

items.title: Onboarding has no interruption, resume, reset, or concurrent-readiness model
items.statement: ATS-020 covers completion, skip, setup failure, and defer paths but not app termination, crash, offline loss, back navigation, repeated setup, reset, account/provider switch, or provider readiness changing while the wizard and Health surfaces are open.
items.impact: Users can re-enter an inconsistent step or see stale Ready/Connected truth after interruption or asynchronous provider changes.

evidence.exact_quote: Tests cover setup completion, setup skip, provider setup failure, auth/logged-in-but-not-ready state, Free Models review

items.title: Onboarding state exclusion rule lacks lifecycle, schema, and hostile-input coverage
items.statement: The minimum fields are merely referenced, while retention, deletion, reset, migration, encryption, access authority, redacted export, field-size limits, and sanitization of provider-controlled labels/errors are not required.
items.impact: A state object can exclude raw credentials yet retain sensitive derived diagnostics indefinitely or render hostile provider text in privileged GUI surfaces.

evidence.exact_quote: - Tests verify onboarding_setup_state contains the accepted minimum fields and excludes raw transcripts, credentials, secrets, and raw diagnostics.

items.title: Exact first-run copy coverage omits accessibility and localization semantics
items.statement: ATS-020 requires exact labels and order but does not test semantic heading/focus order, keyboard traversal, screen-reader status announcements, zoom/reflow, contrast, translated copy, text expansion, locale fallback, or stable semantic identifiers independent of display strings.
items.impact: An English pixel/string test can pass while localized or assistive-technology users cannot understand or operate setup.

evidence.exact_quote: - Tests verify the accepted screen order and exact first-run copy/action labels.

items.title: Cross-document readiness ownership has no staleness or precedence oracle
items.statement: ATS-020 depends on many owner units and surfaces but does not define the authoritative readiness snapshot, version binding, precedence when provider/Health/Doctor/FileSafe disagree, or how consumers invalidate stale cached state.
items.impact: Each subsystem can satisfy its local contract while onboarding presents a contradictory aggregate state.

items.title: Authentication success is explicitly separated from readiness
items.statement: The core directly guards against the principal false-green state by requiring owner readiness proof beyond Connected or Logged in.

evidence.exact_quote: - Do not treat `Connected` or `Logged in` as equivalent to Ready.

items.title: Unresolved DRY owner/source routes have no closure threshold
items.statement: The core labels unresolved owner/source routes exploratory and requires block/ask/open-item behavior for some mutations, but does not state when uncertainty is tolerable, who resolves it, or which terminal evidence closes the caveat. The resulting authority behavior remains underdetermined.
items.impact: Different builders may treat the same unresolved route as warning, block, or implicit authority and all claim conformance.

evidence.exact_quote: visibility, exploratory caveat on unresolved owner/source routes, block/ask/open-item behavior for canonical or

dimension_assessments.summary: Accessible Compact Now callers, future DRY prompt consumers, and readiness consumers lack completeness or discovery oracles.
Compaction event/result transitions, in-flight DRY state, and interrupted onboarding transitions are unspecified.
Cancel/retry, settings writes, host reservations, and asynchronous readiness changes lack race oracles.
Partial compaction, settings persistence, and container cleanup failures are not proven atomic or recoverable.
Rollback and retry contracts are missing for compaction, configuration writes, cleanup, and interrupted onboarding.
DRY-off boundaries are explicit, but bundle authenticity, container isolation, and unresolved-route adjudication remain open.
Usage details, container refs/artifacts, retained failure resources, and onboarding state lack complete lifecycle controls.
Instruction Bundle sources, images/builds/artifacts, access URLs, and provider-controlled onboarding content lack hostile-input tests.
Hover authority and Connected-versus-Ready are closed, but stale async state and failed persistence can still mislead.
Host endpoint loss and onboarding interruption/offline recovery are not covered.
Parallel host capacity, port collisions, evidence sizes, state-field sizes, and resource quotas are unbounded.
Compact Now and first-run tests omit keyboard, screen-reader, focus, reflow, contrast, and non-hover behavior.
Usage/cost presentation and exact onboarding copy lack locale, translation, text-expansion, and semantic-ID coverage.
DRY settings/routes, adapter/receipt versions, and onboarding state schemas lack migration and negotiation contracts.
DRY and container receipts lack fully specified correlation, canonical hashes, time semantics, error codes, and safe diagnostics.
Container cleanup has no scope authorization, idempotency, deletion proof, or retention override contract.
Compact caller parity, adapter-version interoperability, and multi-owner readiness precedence are not defined.
State lists and unspecified receipt fields can be nominally covered without ordering, mutation, provenance, or correlation proof.
The exploratory unresolved-route caveat has no closure owner or evidence threshold, leaving behavior underdetermined.
